description:
THE WRITE-UP IS THE RECORD: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/central/WRITEUP.md (method, both result tables, every caveat, and the ordered NEXT-SESSION list).  All probe files and outputs are beside it (modules.pl, gen.pl, idiom-NN-*.pl, results.txt).

WHY: the suite pass rate (96.5 %) and the cause census rank EXOTIC failures first (Unicode tables, regex engine aborts, &CORE::, the debugger) because perl's t/ tests features in isolation and in bulk; what an ordinary script meets surfaced in s491 only through review probes written in ordinary Perl (eleven pre-existing bugs in one day: #1991 #1870/#1992 #1919 #1751 ...).  The honest instrument is a battery of everyday Perl compared against perl.

NEXT (in order, see the write-up): (1) narrow idiom 33 (POSIX) and idiom 29 (JSON::PP) with stderr visible; (2) File::Copy's refused statement + the Socket AF_UNIX constant (HTTP::Tiny and IO::Socket sit behind it); (3) re-run the six differing idioms with stderr, fix the two probe artifacts; (4) WIDEN the battery before quoting any percentage (list in the write-up, ending with a Moo class and a 100-line real script); (5) PROPOSE to the USER making it an instrument (`tools/everyday-smoke.pl` + a checked-in corpus with perl's expected output, a README-worthy "N of M everyday idioms identical to perl"); (6) only then answer with a number.

ALSO FLAGGED FOR THE USER: the battery shows `@_` aliasing of scalars, array elements and hash elements WORKING (`sub inc { $_[0]++ }` changes the caller's variable in all three) -- the README's "`@_` aliasing: arguments are copies" bullet looks STALE; verify against docs/not-supported.md and tell the USER before touching README prose.

USER STANDING: no new subjobs without asking -- this is Fable's own probing/filing/design work; fixes go to an Opus batch only when launches are allowed.
subject: USER (s491): "how many more central Perl features are failing?" -- an EVERYDAY-PERL battery vs perl, IN PROGRESS: 57 of 73 everyday core modules load; 36 of 42 everyday idioms identical to perl; two differing idioms (POSIX line prints nothing; JSON::PP numbers as strings + `JSON::PP::true` taken as a string) NOT yet narrowed.  USER: "really interesting ... continue looking at this carefully in the next session"
